lens: Boutique recruiter operational fit for finding and reopening the right session/person on a phone

findings.criterion: Retrieval burden and AX5 information grouping
findings.observation: AX5 retains a large two-line count/disclosure region during scrolling, and People adds an initials/menu band before the name. The text remains readable and scrollable, but the shell and redundant identity band reduce the amount of record context visible per viewport.
findings.evidence: 07-sessions-ax5.png, 08-people-ax5.png, 09-sessions-ax5-scrolled.png and 10-people-ax5-scrolled.png; compare compact grouping in 03-people-light.png. review-input.md reports scroll access and restored list anchors after the final source change.
findings.user_impact: Supported inference: a recruiter using the largest text size must spend more attention and scrolling on the same identity/context than the essential text alone requires. The images do not demonstrate a failed retrieval.
findings.recommendation: Reduce nonessential fixed overhead and group the AX5 name/menu more directly; preserve large text, complete context, synthetic disclosure and necessary retrieval controls.
findings.verification: Repeat the four AX5 full-viewport states and the reported anchor/menu tests, then compare time and scrolls to locate a named person and a review-needed session in a realistic long list.

findings.observation: Review needed is explicitly labeled, while unread is primarily a card surface/weight convention. The supplied input explains which records are unread, and CUA reportedly reads the distinction, but the visible surface alone does not name that state.
findings.evidence: 01-sessions-light.png shows two read rows; 02-sessions-unread-light.png elevates Leila while retaining Review needed; 05-sessions-dark-zh.png elevates unread Nia independently of read Leila review attention. These state identities are supplied in review-input.md.
findings.user_impact: Supported inference: on a quick return an unfamiliar recruiter may mistake the elevated row for selection or priority. This is a visual-learning opportunity, not evidence that read state is stored incorrectly.
findings.recommendation: Integrate a concise visible unread cue into the existing metadata while retaining a separate review-attention label.
findings.verification: Ask users to identify unread and review-needed records independently in a five-second light/dark scan without teaching the visual convention; retain the reported state-composition checks.

findings.criterion: Retrieval focus in the complete shell
findings.observation: The light-mode Ask anything composer has a broad shadow and tinted capsule even when the current task is opening an existing record.
findings.evidence: 01-sessions-light.png, 02-sessions-unread-light.png, 03-people-light.png, 04-people-filter.png, 07-sessions-ax5.png and 08-people-ax5.png, including the full bottom shell.
findings.user_impact: Subjective craft inference: the persistent composer introduces a second strong visual focus into an otherwise restrained retrieval page. No accidental action or tap failure is demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Reduce the composer shadow and material emphasis without removing the command or reducing its target.
findings.verification: Compare the full light-mode viewport at compact and AX5 size and confirm the person/topic remains the initial focus while the composer remains discoverable.

strengths: Compact Sessions gives a topic, full person/search context, recency and separately labeled review attention; the input and screenshots distinguish unread from review-needed without conflating them.
Compact People shows full names, employer/role and search context. The single-result filter in 04-people-filter.png names the scope, shows a removal command and truthfully reports one person.
All ten views preserve a quiet two-record or one-record workspace. Sparse space is honest; there are no invented urgency badges, person scores or excessive row glyphs.

AX5 preserves readable text and visible menus. The supplied final behavioral summary reports long-list anchor restoration, compact search and Chinese dark AX5 access, with a hittable first-person menu at least 44 by 44 points.

Scoped behavioral dimension scores: trigger relevance 3; capture burden 3 as applied to intentional search/filter retrieval rather than new evidence capture; state integrity 3 within the stated read-state/identity retrieval scope; interruption recovery 3 on the supplied restoration summary; wedge discipline 3. Evidence review, action usefulness and external-write safety are not scored because these pages do not perform those operations. The minimum material score is 3, not an average or the separate 92/100 craft score.
missing_evidence: No observed recruiter study with realistic search load, interruption, competing work, seeded ambiguity or comparison against the current manual retrieval method; field usefulness and time saved are unproven.
This reviewer did not inspect the raw xcresult bundles or replay the UI. The behavioral evidence is the frozen review-input.md summary, not independent execution by this reviewer.

The stills do not establish VoiceOver conformance, every command target, empty-results reset, all search/filter states, day-later/cross-device recovery, persistence or external-write absence. The reported focused tests support only their stated scope.

The capture-to-evidence-confirmation-to-external-action loop is intentionally outside this review. This pass applies only to the frozen retrieval slice and is not a release approval for that wider loop.
open_questions: Can recruiters using AX5 locate the named person and distinguish unread from review-needed with comparable accuracy after an interruption, without being taught the card convention?
